## Part I
The dataset used for this part is [salaries-by-college-type-clean.csv](../../../dataset/salaries-by-college-type-clean.csv){download="salaries-by-college-type-clean.csv"}. Import the dataset into R.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
df.sal <- read.csv('../../../dataset/salaries-by-college-type-clean.csv')
names(df.sal)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "School.Name"                       "School.Type"                      
[3] "Starting.Median.Salary"            "Mid.Career.Median.Salary"         
[5] "Mid.Career.10th.Percentile.Salary" "Mid.Career.25th.Percentile.Salary"
[7] "Mid.Career.75th.Percentile.Salary" "Mid.Career.90th.Percentile.Salary"
```


:::
:::



1. Look at the variable **Starting.Median.Salary**. Report its 90th, 50th, and 10th percentiles. Provide an interpretation for the 90th percentile.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

The 90th percentile is about $53,660. This means that 10% of schools have a starting median salary above this value, while 90% are at or below it.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
quantile(df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary, c(0.9, 0.5, 0.1))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  90%   50%   10% 
53660 44700 39740 
```


:::
:::


</details>


2. Using relevant information in R to give a thorough description of the variable **Starting.Median.Salary**. Mention properties of *location*, *spread*, and describe the *shape* (i.e., skewness) of the distribution.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

The typical starting median salary is about $44,700 (median), with an average of about $46,068. The highest reported starting median salary is $75,500, from the California Institute of Technology, while the lowest is $34,800, from Morehead State University. The middle 50% of schools have starting median salaries ranging from $42,000 to $48,300. The distribution is right-skewed.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  34800   42000   44700   46068   48300   75500 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
hist(df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](homework_3_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


</details>

3. Calculate the z-scores of **Starting.Median.Salary** and **Mid.Career.Median.Salary** and store the z-scores as separate variables (**zstarting** and **zmid**, respectively) in the data frame.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
df.sal$zstarting <- (df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary - mean(df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary)) / sd(df.sal$Starting.Median.Salary)
df.sal$zmid <- (df.sal$Mid.Career.Median.Salary - mean(df.sal$Mid.Career.Median.Salary)) / sd(df.sal$Mid.Career.Median.Salary)
```
:::


</details>

5. Print the information for *Rutgers University*. Give an interpretation for its **zstarting** and **zmid** values.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

6. What is the mean of **zstarting** for *only the liberal arts colleges*? What about the mean of **zmid** for liberal arts colleges? What conclusion can you draw by comparing the two means?

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mean(df.sal$zstarting[df.sal$School.Type == 'Liberal Arts'])
```

[1] -0.05015004
```

```
